dedupe_keys.name: nist arc alternatives for resilient communities tool

description: NIST ARC is an interactive screening tool, produced by the NIST Community Resilience Systems Modeling team, that helps a community planning team find sets of resilience actions that meet community resilience and cost goals. Given hazard and interdependency information and socio-economic data, it searches decision alternatives across buildings, water, power and transportation systems for a range of natural hazard events, so that planners can see which bridges and buildings to strengthen, which roads, water tanks or power lines to add, and how much backup power and water to hold at hospitals, schools and homes. The tool embeds an optimisation engine, captures redundancy such as backup storage and portable generators, treats mitigation and recovery together, and models recovery with discrete event simulation. Licence (read on the provider page on 2026-09-28): provided as-is (NIST beta software; no licence named). Caveats: it is a beta research tool meant as a starting point for further analysis, and its coverage is a community in the United States as set up by the analyst, with a worked case study. It supports resilience planning and optimisation of interdependent infrastructure; related tools named on the page are IN-CORE and EDGe$, and it complements Hazus in the catalogue. Access is through the provider page linked in this record.
